title: KMS key-wrap orphaning caused missing audit attachments and SSO assertion cross-link failure
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Summary: Several Private deployment customers reported missing audit attachments and gaps in SSO assertion linkage following an automated KMS envelope rotation. The control-plane attempted to rewrap keys while a parallel audit flush was in flight. The race cleared the envelope metadata pointer before the audit service wrote the attachment reference, leaving encrypted blobs orphaned and SSO assertion events without session cross-links. This caused compliance audit failures for at least two customers and triggered an on-call escalation.

Impact: Missing attachments in audit logs (attachments are present in object storage but no corresponding audit entries), and SSO assertion log lines missing 'session_id' references for affected time windows. Customers with strict audit retention and compliance (HIPAA-like) reported inability to prove access-to-data linkage for a small set of requests.

Scope: Affects private control-plane versions that performed envelope rewraps during KMS emergency rekey path between releases runtime-2.2.8 and runtime-2.3.0 when the audit-flush path did not obtain a stable envelope reference. Hosted and Dedicated clusters show different behaviour due to use of managed KMS shim and stronger transactional guarantees; this issue is specific to the private KMS integration path and control-plane rewrap logic.
investigation_summary: 2026-03-10: Customer 'Acme Health' reported missing audit attachments; on-call captured logs and initiated incident INC-2026-0310-1874.
2026-03-10: Reproduced in private staging by forcing a key rotation while issuing closure on pending audit buffer (scripts attached). Repro steps logged in Confluence runbook.
2026-03-11: Root cause narrowed to non-atomic ordering in control-plane: envelope pointer cleared before audit-service write completed when the KMS wrap/unwrapping future resolved with error path.
2026-03-11: Identified secondary symptom: SSO assertion handler looked up envelope metadata to attach session_id linkage; when pointer cleared the handler wrote assertion without session linkage.
2026-03-12: Disk-backed blobs verify existence of encrypted payloads; metadata reconciliation tool can reattach where timestamps align.
2026-03-12: Temporary mitigation applied: disabled auto-rotation for affected private clusters and added extra logging on envelope lifecycle.
2026-03-13: Patch candidate created to make audit write preconditionally reference the existing envelope and to add retry/backoff for rewrap path. PR opened for review.
proposed_fix: Change the control-plane write ordering to ensure audit-service writes the attachment reference before clearing or replacing the envelope pointer (guaranteed write ordering / small transactional lock around envelope metadata).
Add idempotent rewrap path with optimistic concurrency control: keep old envelope reference until new envelope is fully persisted and audit entries confirmed.
Tighten KeyVault client retry behavior to avoid premature error paths during network blips (increase retry window for private KMS endpoints).

Add automatic reconciliation job (one-time migration) to scan orphaned blobs and generate missing audit attachments where a safe mapping can be inferred, with strict rate limiting and operator approval.
testing_plan: Unit tests: cover envelope lifecycle and explicit failure injection during rewrap to assert no metadata is cleared prior to audit write completion.
Integration tests: private-staging cluster with synthetic KMS that simulates latency and transient failures; run full audit flush and rewrap scenarios repeatedly.
E2E: customer-simulated workload replay for Acme Health prompt traces to validate attachments present and SSO assertions contain session_id.
Canary: deploy hotfix to a single private-region customer (non-prod sandbox) for 24 hours and monitor 'audit-missing-attachment' alerts and SSO linkage metrics.
Regression: run existing audit-performance and key-rotation load tests to ensure <2% latency regression and no increase in error rates.
Manual verification steps documented for on-call to validate reattached items post-migration.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR to platform branch and build runtime-2.3.1-hotfix image.
2) Deploy to private-staging and run automated integration suite (target 1 hour).
3) Canary deploy to 1 customer sandbox region for 24h with tight telemetry (audit write success, SSO linkage ratio, KMS error rate).
4) If canary stable, roll to remaining private clusters in waves of 10% of capacity with automatic pause on regressions for human review.
5) After full rollout, run reconciliation job against blob store for the affected time window and create audit attachments where mapping is safe. Notify customers and provide verification report.
rollback_plan: Revert runtime image to previous stable tag (runtime-2.2.8) and restart control-plane; this will restore prior envelope handling semantics.
If rollback performed after migration run, mark any auto-generated attachments with 'migration:revert' tag and prepare for manual clean-up as necessary.
Notify impacted customers and open follow-up support tickets to validate audit continuity.
acceptance_criteria: No new 'missing-audit-attachment' incidents observed in canary window (24h), and metric 'audit.attachment_written_success_rate' >= 99.9%.
SSO assertion linkage ratio restored to baseline (session_id present in >= 99.95% of assertion events).
Unit + integration + e2e tests pass in CI for private KMS paths.
Security review completed and signoff from Security team documented in PR.
Reconciliation job completes and reconciled items are validated by on-call on a sample set.
customer_contacts: Harbor Medical - security@harbormed.example (secondary, observed similar traces)
Acme Health compliance lead: Marina Ortiz
notes: Trade-offs: Implementing a full transactional store for envelope metadata would be higher assurance but would add substantial infra work and risk to rollout; chosen pragmatic fix is ordering + idempotency + reconciliation job.
Performance: locking around envelope write kept as a micro-lock scoped to single envelope ID to minimize contention; estimated <2% p99 latency impact based on load tests.
Operator safety: reconciliation job will be run with dry-run first and requires explicit operator confirmation and customer opt-in for auto-reattach of audit entries.
Regulatory: Security team flagged that any auto-generated attachment must be clearly labeled and auditable; added tags and provenance metadata to migration outputs.
